rationale:
Split into two children. Both are comparator-accepted DAG declarations, reused with byte-identical frozen types, so no new node and no new proof obligation is created:
- im_series = Submission.cmcdt_im_series (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.deformation_theorem-a1.im_series-a1, candidate 9b823b5);
- lipschitz_piece_current = Submission.dimred_mbl_dt_lpip_lipschitz_piece_current (node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.moving_blowups-a1.deformation_theorem-a1.lipschitz_pushforward-a1.im_pushforward-a1.piece_current-a1, candidate 918eb38).

Why split. The supplied proof carries a wiring requirement. These two declarations are neither siblings of this node nor in its proof base (4e261d7). An unsplit leaf could use only VO, MR and IMC, and would have to reprove Simon 6.3.9 for Lipschitz pieces and 6.3.13 for M-summable series, i.e. thousands of lines of accepted Lean. The split is the genuine factorization of the integrality in Simon 6.3.10 (chapter-06.txt lines 864–866): each Lipschitz piece is integer multiplicity (6.3.3–3.9, lines 770–862), and an M-summable series of integer multiplicity currents is integer multiplicity (6.3.13, lines 901–935).

- Step 1 → im_series: IMS := cmcdt_im_series VO MR IMC.
- Step 2 → lipschitz_piece_current, applied to MR, IMC, IMS and to P, k, L_i (from ∃ L), G_i, A_i, w_i. Measurability of A_i and w_i and integrability of w_i on A_i are hypotheses of the selected statement.

  - IMS applied to (S_i);
  - HasSum.unique and GeometricCurrentOn.ext give T = S.
- VO, MR and IMC are deliberately not children. They are this node's declared dependencies (vanish_off_support-a1, mass_equals_rep_measure-a1, im_calculus-a1, all accepted). runtime.py `_overlay_accepted_children` merges the accepted candidates of [*node.children, *node.depends_on] before the parent's implementation base is pinned. subproblems.title: Mass-summable series of currents; integer multiplicity of sums of integer multiplicity currents
subproblems.statement: Assume, as hypotheses of the statement, (VO) the frozen type of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support: for all P, n, U, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0; (MR) the frozen type of Submission.cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure: for U open and an IMRep R representing T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W; (IMC) the frozen type of Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for Borel M ⊆ M' ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ (K ⊆ U compact); (b) the restriction (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) of an IMRep to a Borel E is an IMRep representing some current; (c) A − B is integer multiplicity for integer multiplicity A, B (U open); (d) |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ-a.e. x in the carrier. (These are exactly the frozen Lean types of the parent node's resolved dependencies, written as antecedents so that the child does not need those declarations; the parent instantiates them.) Let P, k ∈ ℕ and W_i ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) (i ∈ ℕ, domain univ) with Σ_i M(W_i) < ∞ (tsum in [0, ∞]). Then there is S ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) such that: for every test form ω, the series Σ_i W_i(ω) has sum S(ω) (HasSum); M(S) ≤ Σ_i M(W_i); spt S ⊆ closure(⋃_i spt W_i); and if every W_i is integer multiplicity then S is integer multiplicity.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) → ((∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M M' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet M → MeasurableSet M' → M ⊆ M' → M' ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (M' ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet E → ∃ (A : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents A ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α)) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (W : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1)), ∑' i, (W i).mass < ∞ → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1), (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1), HasSum (fun i => W i ω) (S ω)) ∧ S.mass ≤ ∑' i, (W i).mass ∧ S.support ⊆ closure (⋃ i, (W i).support) ∧ ((∀ i, IsIntegerMultiplicity (W i)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity S)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof): this child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmcdt_im_series of DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.deformation_theorem-a1.im_series-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 9b823b56965f653716675d2e458c314229939386). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above. It was copied from dag.json and occurs verbatim as `theorem Submission.cmcdt_im_series : <type> :=` in that commit, whose only sorry is the frozen root main_theorem and which declares no axioms. dag.json has no other node with this name, so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Use in the selected node: step 1 of the parent proof. Applied to the selected node's declared dependencies (VO) = Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support, (MR) = Submission.cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure and (IMC) = Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, it gives the statement IMS. IMS discharges the antecedent (IMSc) of the sibling lipschitz_piece_current (parent step 2) and sums the pieces S_i (parent step 5).

Accepted proof (the accepted node's parent-supplied natural proof, verbatim except for the source line):

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13 (chapter-06.txt lines 901–935: integer multiplicity currents are complete for the semi-norms M_W), specialised to an M-absolutely summable series, together with the elementary fact that mass-summable series of currents define currents. Countably many integer multiplicity pieces whose multiplicities have finite total integral are combined into one integer multiplicity current. This uses the locality of approximate tangent spaces ((IMC)(a)) and the sign rule (L3) proved in (5d). In the accepted node this argument is the closing step of B3 of the deformation-theorem proof, where it replaces Simon 3.13.

Notation. All currents are in 𝒟_{n'}(ℝ^P) with domain univ, n' := k + 1. ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| (Euclidean coefficient norm). Hypotheses (VO), (MR), (IMC) are the three displayed hypotheses of the statement (frozen types of Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub).

1. Evaluation bound. For every current X and test form ω, |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ (in [0, ∞]). Indeed, if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0; otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ are admissible for M(X) (support in univ, |·| ≤ 1), so ±X(ω)/‖ω‖ ≤ M(X).

2. Definition of S. Let Σ_i M(W_i) =: A < ∞. For each ω, Σ_i |W_i(ω)| ≤ A‖ω‖ < ∞, so S(ω) := Σ_i W_i(ω) converges absolutely; in particular HasSum (i ↦ W_i(ω)) (S(ω)). S is linear. Continuity: if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology (supports in one compact set, all derivatives → 0 uniformly), then sup_x of the operator norm of ω_j(x) tends to 0. The Euclidean coefficient norm is bounded by a constant C(P, n') times the operator norm (each coefficient ω(x)(e_{i_1},…,e_{i_{n'}}) is bounded by the operator norm). Hence ‖ω_j‖ → 0 and |S(ω_j)| ≤ A‖ω_j‖ → 0. So S ∈ 𝒟_{n'}(ℝ^P).

3. Mass. For admissible ω, S(ω) = Σ_i W_i(ω) ≤ Σ_i M(W_i), so M(S) ≤ Σ_i M(W_i).

4. Support. Let E := closure ⋃_i spt W_i and x ∉ E. Choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ∩ E = ∅. The open ball B := ball(x, r) has compact closure. Every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B satisfies tsupport ω ∩ spt W_i = ∅ for all i, hence W_i(ω) = 0 by (VO) and S(ω) = 0. So x lies in the zero region of S, i.e. spt S ⊆ E.

5. Integer multiplicity. Assume every W_i is integer multiplicity, with IMRep R_i = (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i). By (MR) (U = W = univ, open), ∫_{M_i} θ_i dH^{n'} = R_i.measure(ℝ^P) = M(W_i). Modifying ξ_i on an H^{n'}⌞M_i-null set, we may take ξ_i Borel (this changes neither the action nor the a.e. orientation property).
 (5a) N := ⋃_i M_i is Borel and countably n'-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion), and H^{n'}(N) ≤ Σ_i H^{n'}(M_i) ≤ Σ_i ∫_{M_i}θ_i dH^{n'} = A < ∞ because θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i.
 (5b) Θ := Σ_i θ_i 1_{M_i} : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] has ∫ Θ dH^{n'} = A, so Θ < ∞ off an H^{n'}-null set. At such points only finitely many i have x ∈ M_i (θ_i ≥ 1 there).
 (5c) Tangent planes. For each i, apply (IMC)(a) with U = univ, M = M_i ⊆ M' = N (H^{n'}(N ∩ K) ≤ A < ∞): for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ M_i and every subspace Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n' M_i x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n' N x Q. By the orientation field of R_i, for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ M_i there is Q_i(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n' M_i x Q_i(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_i(x)) (Q_i(x)). Removing a countable union of null sets, for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ N each i with x ∈ M_i gives an approximate tangent space Q_i(x) of N at x. By uniqueness (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) these coincide; call the common value Q(x).
 (5d) Signs. Let ι(x) := min{i : x ∈ M_i} for x ∈ N (Borel) and η(x) := ξ_{ι(x)}(x) (Borel). (L3) Two unit orientations of the same n'-dimensional subspace differ by a sign: if ξ = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) and ξ' = ±(α ↦ α(τ')) with orthonormal bases τ, τ' of Q, then τ' = Oτ for an orthogonal O, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Put s_i(x) := 1 if ‖ξ_i(x) − η(x)‖ ≤ ‖ξ_i(x) + η(x)‖ and s_i(x) := −1 otherwise (Borel). A unit orientation is nonzero (it takes the value ±1 on a covector dual to its orthonormal frame). So for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ N and every i with x ∈ M_i, ξ_i(x) = s_i(x)η(x).
 (5e) Multiplicity. m(x) := Σ_i s_i(x)θ_i(x)1_{M_i}(x) (set m := 0 where Θ(x) = ∞) is Borel, as a pointwise limit of finite sums of Borel integer-valued functions. H^{n'}-a.e. on N it is a finite sum of integers, and |m| ≤ Θ, so m is integer-valued a.e. with ∫|m| dH^{n'} ≤ A.
 (5f) Action. For a test form ω, |ξ_i(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ ‖ω‖ for a.e. x ∈ M_i ((IMC)(d)), so Σ_i ∫ θ_i 1_{M_i}|ξ_i(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖A. Dominated convergence for series gives
 S(ω) = Σ_i ∫_{M_i} θ_i ξ_i(x)(ω(x)) dH^{n'} = ∫_N Σ_i θ_i 1_{M_i} s_i η(x)(ω(x)) dH^{n'} = ∫_N m(x) η(x)(ω(x)) dH^{n'}.
 (5g) The IMRep. Let Z ⊆ N be a Borel H^{n'}-null set outside of which (5b)–(5e) hold. Put N' := {x ∈ N ∖ Z : m(x) ≠ 0} (Borel), mult := |m| on N' and 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued, positive on N'), and orient := sign(m)η. Check the IMRep fields:
 - N' ⊆ univ;
 - N' ⊆ N is countably n'-rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono);
 - local integrability: ∫_{N'∩K}|m| ≤ A < ∞;
 - orient is Borel;
 - for H^{n'}-a.e. x ∈ N', (IMC)(a) with M = N' ⊆ M' = N gives that Q(x), an approximate tangent space of N at x, is also one of N' at x, and sign(m(x))η(x) is a unit orientation of Q(x) (the definition IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign).
 Its action is ∫_{N'} |m| sign(m) η(ω) dH^{n'} = ∫_N m η(ω) dH^{n'} = S(ω) (m = 0 on N ∖ (N' ∪ Z)). Hence S is integer multiplicity.

6. The current S of 2 satisfies the four conclusions by 2, 3, 4 and 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: Evaluation bound |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖ (‖ω‖ = sup of the Euclidean coefficient norm), so S(ω) := Σ_i W_i(ω) converges absolutely and is a sequentially continuous linear functional; HasSum holds for every ω.
M(S) ≤ Σ_i M(W_i) by evaluating on admissible forms; spt S ⊆ closure ⋃ spt W_i, because (VO) kills every W_i on forms supported in a ball missing that closure.
For integer multiplicity W_i with IMReps (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i): by (MR), Σ_i ∫_{M_i}θ_i dH = Σ_i M(W_i) < ∞, so N := ⋃ M_i has finite measure and a.e. x lies in only finitely many M_i.
By (IMC)(a) and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, all M_i containing x share the tangent space of N at x. The sign rule (L3) gives ξ_i = s_i η for a Borel reference orientation η.
m := Σ_i s_i θ_i 1_{M_i} is integer-valued a.e. with ∫|m| ≤ Σ M(W_i). Dominated convergence gives S(ω) = ∫_N m η(ω) dH, and (N', |m|, sign(m)η) with N' := {m ≠ 0} minus a null set is an IMRep of S.

subproblems.title: Integrality of the Lipschitz image of an integer-weighted Lebesgue piece (supplied step 5(a), 5(d))
subproblems.statement: Assume (MR), (IMC) and (IMSc). (MR) is the exact frozen type of the accepted Submission.cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure: for U open, an IMRep R in U representing T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and every open W, M_W(T) = T.massOn W = R.measure W. (IMC) is the exact frozen type of the accepted Submission.cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, the conjunction of: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces: for U ⊆ ℝ^P open and Borel M ⊆ M' ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every subspace Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q; (b) restriction: for U open, an IMRep R in U and a Borel set E there are a current A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R' with R'.Represents A, R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R'.mult = R.mult, R'.orient = R.orient; (c) A − B is integer multiplicity if A, B are (U open); (d) for every IMRep R, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier and every n-covector α, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α. (IMSc) is the conclusion of the frozen type of Submission.dimred_mbl_dt_im_series (the selected node's (IMS) after discharging its antecedents (VO), (MR), (IMC)): for all P, k and W : ℕ → 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with Σ_l M(W_l) < ∞ there is S ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with HasSum (l ↦ W_l(ω)) (S(ω)) for every test form ω, M(S) ≤ Σ_l M(W_l), spt S ⊆ closure ⋃_l spt W_l, and S is integer multiplicity if every W_l is. It is a declared dependency of the accepted node, and its commit is an ancestor of 918eb38. Its frozen type states the following. Assume (MR) and (IMC). Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and κ > 0. Let H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz and A' ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel, with κ|a − a'| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| for a, a' ∈ A'. Assume H is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of A', and g : ℝⁿ → ℤ is measurable, nonzero on A' and Lebesgue integrable on A'. Then there is an integer multiplicity Φ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) such that Φ(ω) = ∫_{A'} g(u)·ω(H u)(DH(u)e_0, …, DH(u)e_{n−1}) du for every test form ω, and M(Φ) ≤ Lⁿ·∫⁻_{A'} |g| dλ.
1. (Integrability.) ‖DH(u)‖ ≤ L for all u (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz), so |DH(u)e_a| ≤ L. ω is continuous with compact support, so C_ω := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (operator norm) and |ω(y)(z)| ≤ ‖ω(y)‖∏_a|z_a|. Ψ_ω is Borel (g measurable, H continuous, u ↦ DH(u) Borel by measurable_fderiv, (y, z) ↦ ω(y)(z) continuous) and |Ψ_ω| ≤ C_ωLⁿ|g|, so Ψ_ω is integrable on A.
2. (Regular part.) Let A⁺ := {u ∈ A : DH(u) injective, g(u) ≠ 0}. Since n = k + 1 ≥ 1, DH(u) = 0 is not injective where H is not differentiable (fderiv is 0 there), so H is differentiable at every u ∈ A⁺. A⁺ is Borel: DH(u) is injective iff v(u) is linearly independent (DH(u) maps the standard basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun to v(u)), the set of linearly independent families in (ℝ^P)^n is open (isOpen_setOfPred_linearIndependent) and u ↦ v(u) is Borel (measurable_fderiv); equivalently DH(u) is injective iff J_H(u) ≠ 0 (the accepted Submission.codim1_lur_normalized_wedge_orientation gives det Gram(v) > 0, so J_H > 0, for independent v; for dependent v, Gram(v)·c = 0 for some c ≠ 0, so det = 0), and J_H is Borel by part (i) of the accepted Submission.codim1_lura_gram_area_formula. For u ∈ A ∖ A⁺, either g(u) = 0, or DH(u) is not injective, so v(u) is linearly dependent and ω(H u)(v(u)) = 0 (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent applied to the alternating map underlying ω(H u)); in both cases Ψ_ω(u) = 0. Hence ∫_A Ψ_ω = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω (no Rademacher theorem is needed).
3. (Bi-Lipschitz partition, supplied 5(a).) For an injective linear T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P choose K_T > 0 with |w| ≤ K_T|Tw| for all w (LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith) and put r(T) := (2K_T)⁻¹; put r(T) := 1 if T is not injective; so r(T) ≠ 0 for all T. H has derivative DH(u) within A⁺ at each u ∈ A⁺, so exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (f := H, s := A⁺, f' := DH, r) gives pairwise disjoint Borel t_l (l ∈ ℕ) with A⁺ ⊆ ⋃_l t_l and linear T_l with |H(u) − H(u') − T_l(u − u')| ≤ r(T_l)|u − u'| for u, u' ∈ A⁺ ∩ t_l, and, if A⁺ ≠ ∅, T_l = DH(y_l) for some y_l ∈ A⁺ (so T_l is injective). Put A_l := A⁺ ∩ t_l (Borel, pairwise disjoint, ⋃_l A_l = A⁺) and κ_l := (2K_{T_l})⁻¹ if A⁺ ≠ ∅, κ_l := 1 otherwise (then every A_l is empty). For u, u' ∈ A_l: |H(u) − H(u')| ≥ |T_l(u − u')| − r(T_l)|u − u'| ≥ (K_{T_l}⁻¹ − (2K_{T_l})⁻¹)|u − u'| = κ_l|u − u'|.
4. (Pieces.) For each l apply BIC (step 0, with (MR), (IMC); P, n, L, κ_l, H, A' := A_l, g): H is L-Lipschitz, A_l is Borel, κ_l > 0, the bi-Lipschitz bound is step 3, H is differentiable with injective derivative on A_l ⊆ A⁺, g is measurable, nonzero on A_l and integrable on A_l ⊆ A. It gives an integer multiplicity Φ_l with Φ_l(ω) = ∫_{A_l} Ψ_ω for every test form ω and M(Φ_l) ≤ Lⁿ∫⁻_{A_l}|g| dλ.
5. (Summable masses.) Σ_l M(Φ_l) ≤ Lⁿ Σ_l ∫⁻_{A_l}|g| = Lⁿ∫⁻_{A⁺}|g| (lintegral_iUnion, disjoint Borel A_l) ≤ Lⁿ∫⁻_A|g| < ∞.
6. (IMS.) (IMSc) with P, k and W_l := Φ_l gives S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with HasSum (l ↦ Φ_l(ω)) (S(ω)) for every test form ω; S is integer multiplicity because every Φ_l is.
7. (Identification.) For a test form ω, Ψ_ω is integrable on A⁺ (step 1), so HasSum (l ↦ ∫_{A_l} Ψ_ω) (∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω) (hasSum_integral_iUnion). By step 4 and uniqueness of sums (HasSum.unique), S(ω) = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω = ∫_A Ψ_ω (step 2) = ∫_A g(u)ω(H u)(DH(u)e) du. ∎

Ψ_ω = g·ω(H)(DH e) is integrable on A and vanishes off A⁺ = {DH injective, g ≠ 0}. A⁺ is Borel: fderiv = 0 off the differentiability set and n ≥ 1, and alternating maps vanish on dependent vectors.
Mathlib's approximately-linear partition, with r(T) half the coercivity constant of T, splits A⁺ into disjoint Borel pieces A_l on which H is bi-Lipschitz.
BIC gives integer multiplicity Φ_l with Φ_l(ω) = ∫_{A_l}Ψ_ω and M(Φ_l) ≤ Lⁿ∫⁻_{A_l}|g|, so Σ_l M(Φ_l) ≤ Lⁿ∫⁻_A|g| < ∞.
(IMSc) sums the Φ_l to an integer multiplicity S. Countable additivity (hasSum_integral_iUnion) and HasSum.unique identify S(ω) = ∫_A Ψ_ω.
